newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stabilised, tone biddish on dlr.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stabilised, tone biddish on dlr.

text.p: Indonesia's rupiah stabilised against the dollar late in the afternoon on Thursday after it was jolted by a report that President Suharto had suffered a minor heart ailment on Wednesday, dealers said.

Foreign Minister Ali Alatas said after meeting Suharto on Thursday that rumours about the president's health were not true. "You can see yourself the president is performing his full duties," he told reporters at the presidential palace.
The rupiah dropped to a low of 2,420 overnight in New York before settling at 2,405. It was traded in a range between 2,402 and 2,405 in Jakarta on Thursday with the market in a jumpy mood.
Spot rupiah settled at 2,403.25/04.00 at 0900 GMT against an opening of 2,402.0/06.0. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,402.25/03.00 and 2,401.00/01.75, respectively.
Dealers said the market had calmed down for now, but players were still cautious as the market remained sensitive and volatile on rumours linked to Suharto's health.
"The market is a bit choppy. The underlying tone for dollars is a bit biddish," one local bank dealer said.
He said operators were a bit wary of the liquidity outlook ahead of the new reserve rate.
"Overnight money was relatively stable throughout the day. This could be a kind of signal," the dealer said.
Overnight money was hovering at 11.0/12.0 percent.
Another dealer said some players seemed to speculate on a liquidity tightening or even a band widening which helped compensate pressure on the rupiah.
He said many operators were short on dollars before on expectation for a tight liquidity on Thursday.
Dealers said swap rates were little moved in the afternoon.
Tom/next swap was at 0.85/0.95 and spot/next at 0.25/0.35.
One-month swaps were at 11.50/11.75, two at 23.5/24.5, three at 34.5/35.5 and six at 70.5/71.0 points.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by one point to 2,395/2,587 and the conversion band to 2,395/2,443 on Thursday.
One currency dealer in Singapore said earlier dollar buying in the afternoon might be due to short-covering.
Some economists attributed the sharp overnight drop to the unsolved succesion issue in Indonesia.
"There are definite worries over the succession issue. I think that is the major concern," a senior banker said.

"The political issue really is the key risk in Indonesia. Taking the economy as a whole, things are actually looking good," Desmond Supple, head of research for Asian Currency at BZW in Singapore, said on Thursday.
"There is no balance of payment risk. The economy is looking extremely strong and the rupiah has been under a lot of upside pressure in recent years," Supple said.
"The key concern is politics," he added.
Supple said the rupiah would remain susceptible to periodic bouts of weakness because of political concerns.
But Supple said: "Even taking on board the political risks, the currency was still looking attractive."
